review_note: Retains that surjective flat scheme map is an epimorphism in the categorical sense: precomposition detects equality of any two scheme maps, with no unnecessary quasi-compactness.
statement: Let $h:X'\to X$ be a surjective flat morphism of schemes. Then $h$ is an epimorphism in the category of schemes: for any scheme $Y$ and maps $a,b:X\to Y$, equality $a\circ h=b\circ h$ implies $a=b$. No quasi-compactness hypothesis is required.
conclusions: h is a categorical epimorphism of schemes.

review_note: Preserves faithfulness of base-change Sch/S→Sch/S' for surjective flat S'→S. The canonical comparison detects equality of morphisms and need not be full.
statement: Let $h:S'\to S$ be a surjective flat morphism of schemes. Then scalar extension $(-)\times_SS':\operatorname{Sch}/S\to\operatorname{Sch}/S'$ is a faithful functor: if two $S$-morphisms $a,b:X\to Y$ become equal after base change to $S'$, then $a=b$.
hypotheses: h is surjective flat; a,b morphisms over S.
conclusions: Base extension along h reflects equality of morphisms.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-ff-base-change-faithful}
Let $h : S' \to S$ be a surjective, flat morphism of
schemes. The base change functor
$$
\Sch/S \longrightarrow \Sch/S', \quad
X \longmapsto S' \times_S X
$$
is faithful.

review_note: Retains faithfulness of pullback DD(X/S)→DD(X'/S) under f:X'→X surjective flat, with source/target of f and S fixed; no fpqc/quasi-compact assumption added.
statement: Fix $p:X\to S$. Write $\mathrm{DD}(X/S)$ for the category of descent data for schemes along $X\to S$. An object is a scheme $V\to X$ and an isomorphism $\varphi:V\times_S X\xrightarrow{\sim} X\times_SV$ over $X\times_SX$ satisfying the cocycle identity on $X\times_SX\times_SX$. Morphisms are $X$-morphisms compatible with these isomorphisms. For a morphism $f:X'\to X$ over $S$, pullback is the functor $f^*:\mathrm{DD}(X/S)\to\mathrm{DD}(X'/S)$ taking $V$ to $V\times_X X'$ and $\varphi$ to its pullback along $f\times_Sf$. Let $f:X'\to X$ be a surjective flat morphism over $S$. Then the pullback functor $f^*:\mathrm{DD}(X/S)\to\mathrm{DD}(X'/S)$ is faithful: two morphisms of descent data that become equal after pullback were already equal.
hypotheses: f:X'→X over S is surjective and flat.
conclusions: Pullback of schemes with descent data along f is faithful.

review_note: Retains FULL faithfulness of descent-data pullback for f:X'→X an fpqc covering over the same S. Explicitly distinguishes full faithfulness from effectivity of all descent objects.
statement: Fix $p:X\to S$. Write $\mathrm{DD}(X/S)$ for the category of descent data for schemes along $X\to S$. An object is a scheme $V\to X$ and an isomorphism $\varphi:V\times_S X\xrightarrow{\sim} X\times_SV$ over $X\times_SX$ satisfying the cocycle identity on $X\times_SX\times_SX$. Morphisms are $X$-morphisms compatible with these isomorphisms. For a morphism $f:X'\to X$ over $S$, pullback is the functor $f^*:\mathrm{DD}(X/S)\to\mathrm{DD}(X'/S)$ taking $V$ to $V\times_X X'$ and $\varphi$ to its pullback along $f\times_Sf$. Assume $f:X'\to X$ is an fpqc covering (for example, $f$ is surjective, flat, and quasi-compact) and both objects $X,X'$ are regarded over the same scheme $S$. Then the pullback functor $f^*:\mathrm{DD}(X/S)\to\mathrm{DD}(X'/S)$ is fully faithful: every compatible morphism between pulled-back descent data descends uniquely to a morphism before pullback. This is a statement about morphisms of descent data, not the effectivity of every object.
hypotheses: f:X'→X is an fpqc covering; the base scheme S is unchanged.
conclusions: The pullback functor on categories of scheme descent data is fully faithful.

review_note: Preserves natural isomorphism f*:DD(X/S)→DD(X/S) to identity for ANY S-selfmap f:X→X, relying on the descent datum to identify resulting presentations.
statement: Fix $p:X\to S$. Write $\mathrm{DD}(X/S)$ for the category of descent data for schemes along $X\to S$. An object is a scheme $V\to X$ and an isomorphism $\varphi:V\times_S X\xrightarrow{\sim} X\times_SV$ over $X\times_SX$ satisfying the cocycle identity on $X\times_SX\times_SX$. Morphisms are $X$-morphisms compatible with these isomorphisms. For a morphism $f:X'\to X$ over $S$, pullback is the functor $f^*:\mathrm{DD}(X/S)\to\mathrm{DD}(X'/S)$ taking $V$ to $V\times_X X'$ and $\varphi$ to its pullback along $f\times_Sf$. If $f:X\to X$ is any morphism over $S$, then $f^*:\mathrm{DD}(X/S)\to\mathrm{DD}(X/S)$ is naturally isomorphic to the identity functor. The isomorphism uses the descent datum to identify changes of the chosen presentation map $X\to S$.
hypotheses: f is an S-selfmap of X.
conclusions: Pullback along f on DD(X/S) is naturally isomorphic to the identity.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-pullback-selfmap}
Let $X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $f : X \to X$ be a selfmap of $X$ over $S$.
In this case pullback by $f$ is isomorphic to the
identity functor on the category of descent data
relative to $X \to S$.

review_note: Retains the unusual source premise: there merely exists an S-morphism g:X→X' reverse to f:X'→X, not necessarily a section. Then f* is equivalence of descent-data categories via g* and selfmap invariance.
statement: Fix $p:X\to S$. Write $\mathrm{DD}(X/S)$ for the category of descent data for schemes along $X\to S$. An object is a scheme $V\to X$ and an isomorphism $\varphi:V\times_S X\xrightarrow{\sim} X\times_SV$ over $X\times_SX$ satisfying the cocycle identity on $X\times_SX\times_SX$. Morphisms are $X$-morphisms compatible with these isomorphisms. For a morphism $f:X'\to X$ over $S$, pullback is the functor $f^*:\mathrm{DD}(X/S)\to\mathrm{DD}(X'/S)$ taking $V$ to $V\times_X X'$ and $\varphi$ to its pullback along $f\times_Sf$. Let $f:X'\to X$ be a morphism of schemes over $S$. Assume there exists an $S$-morphism $g:X\to X'$ (in particular, a section of $f$ suffices, but $f\circ g=\mathrm{id}_X$ is not required). Then $f^*:\mathrm{DD}(X/S)\to\mathrm{DD}(X'/S)$ is an equivalence of categories, with quasi-inverse $g^*$, since both composites are pullbacks by $S$-selfmaps and hence naturally isomorphic to the identity.
hypotheses: f:X'→X over S admits any reverse S-map g:X→X'.
conclusions: The induced pullback functor on descent-data categories is an equivalence.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-morphism-with-section-equivalence}
Let $f : X' \to X$ be a morphism of schemes over a base scheme $S$.
Assume there exists a morphism $g : X \to X'$ over $S$, for example
if $f$ has a section. Then the pullback functor
of Lemma \ref{lemma-pullback} defines an equivalence of
categories between the category of descent data relative to
$X/S$ and $X'/S$.

review_note: Preserves faithful pullback DD(X'/S)→DD(X/S) when f:X→X' over S and STRUCTURE morphism X→S is surjective flat, without wrongly asserting f itself surjective.
statement: Fix $p:X\to S$. Write $\mathrm{DD}(X/S)$ for the category of descent data for schemes along $X\to S$. An object is a scheme $V\to X$ and an isomorphism $\varphi:V\times_S X\xrightarrow{\sim} X\times_SV$ over $X\times_SX$ satisfying the cocycle identity on $X\times_SX\times_SX$. Morphisms are $X$-morphisms compatible with these isomorphisms. For a morphism $f:X'\to X$ over $S$, pullback is the functor $f^*:\mathrm{DD}(X/S)\to\mathrm{DD}(X'/S)$ taking $V$ to $V\times_X X'$ and $\varphi$ to its pullback along $f\times_Sf$. Let $f:X\to X'$ be an $S$-morphism. Assume the structure map $X\to S$ is surjective and flat. Then pullback $f^*:\mathrm{DD}(X'/S)\to\mathrm{DD}(X/S)$ is faithful, even without requiring $f$ itself to be surjective or flat.
hypotheses: f:X→X' is an S-map; the structure morphism X→S is surjective and flat.
conclusions: The induced pullback on descent data is faithful.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-morphism-source-faithfully-flat}
Let $f : X \to X'$ be a morphism of schemes over a base scheme $S$.
Assume $X \to S$ is surjective and flat. Then the pullback functor
of Lemma \ref{lemma-pullback} is a faithful functor
from the category of descent data relative to $X'/S$ to the
category of descent data relative to $X/S$.

review_note: Preserves full faithfulness under a morphism of covering families with each subfamily {Ui→Vj | α(i)=j} fpqc over Vj. The indexed refinement and category directions DD(V)→DD(U) stay intact.
statement: For a family $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to S\}$, let $\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal U)$ be the category of families of $U_i$-schemes $V_i$ together with isomorphisms $\varphi_{ij}:V_i\times_SU_j\xrightarrow{\sim}U_i\times_SV_j$ over $U_i\times_SU_j$ satisfying the cocycle condition on triple overlaps. A morphism of families $(\alpha,g_i):\mathcal U\to\mathcal V=\{V_j\to S\}$ comprises a function $\alpha:I\to J$ and maps $g_i:U_i\to V_{\alpha(i)}$ over $S$; it induces a pullback functor $\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal V)\to\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal U)$. Assume for each $j\in J$ the subfamily $\{g_i:U_i\to V_j\mid\alpha(i)=j\}$ is an fpqc covering of $V_j$. Then the induced pullback $\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal V)\to\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal U)$ is fully faithful. The underlying morphism of disjoint unions $\coprod_iU_i\to\coprod_jV_j$ is an fpqc covering, and the family-to-coproduct equivalence identifies the indicated pullback with pullback along that morphism.
hypotheses: Each fibre of the index map alpha gives an fpqc cover of the corresponding V_j.
conclusions: Refinement pullback on descent-data categories is fully faithful.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-fpqc-refinement-coverings-fully-faithful}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to S\}_{i \in I}$, and
$\mathcal{V} = \{V_j \to S\}_{j \in J}$,
be families of morphisms with target $S$.
Let $\alpha : I \to J$, $\text{id} : S \to S$ and
$g_i : U_i \to V_{\alpha(i)}$ be a morphism of families
of maps with fixed target, see
Sites, Definition \ref{sites-definition-morphism-coverings}.
Assume that for each $j \in J$ the family
$\{g_i : U_i \to V_j\}_{\alpha(i) = j}$ is an fpqc
covering of $V_j$. Then the pullback functor
$$
\text{descent data relative to }
\mathcal{V}
\longrightarrow
\text{descent data relative to }
\mathcal{U}
$$
of Lemma \ref{lemma-pullback-family} is fully faithful.

review_note: Retains equivalence (not merely fully faithful) of scheme descent categories when each refining subfamily is a Zariski open covering; also preserves gluing of schemes from any Zariski descent datum.
statement: For a family $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to S\}$, let $\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal U)$ be the category of families of $U_i$-schemes $V_i$ together with isomorphisms $\varphi_{ij}:V_i\times_SU_j\xrightarrow{\sim}U_i\times_SV_j$ over $U_i\times_SU_j$ satisfying the cocycle condition on triple overlaps. A morphism of families $(\alpha,g_i):\mathcal U\to\mathcal V=\{V_j\to S\}$ comprises a function $\alpha:I\to J$ and maps $g_i:U_i\to V_{\alpha(i)}$ over $S$; it induces a pullback functor $\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal V)\to\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal U)$. Suppose for every $j\in J$ the subfamily $\{g_i:U_i\to V_j\mid\alpha(i)=j\}$ is a Zariski open covering of $V_j$. Then pullback $\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal V)\to\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal U)$ is an equivalence of categories, not just fully faithful. In particular, if $\{U_i\to S\}$ is any Zariski open covering, $\operatorname{Sch}/S$ is equivalent to the category of scheme descent data for this cover, via ordinary gluing.
hypotheses: The refinement is, on each V_j, a Zariski open covering.
conclusions: The induced pullback is an equivalence; schemes descend effectively along Zariski covers.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-Zariski-refinement-coverings-equivalence}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to S\}_{i \in I}$, and
$\mathcal{V} = \{V_j \to S\}_{j \in J}$,
be families of morphisms with target $S$.
Let $\alpha : I \to J$, $\text{id} : S \to S$ and
$g_i : U_i \to V_{\alpha(i)}$ be a morphism of families
of maps with fixed target, see
Sites, Definition \ref{sites-definition-morphism-coverings}.
Assume that for each $j \in J$ the family
$\{g_i : U_i \to V_j\}_{\alpha(i) = j}$ is a Zariski covering (see
Topologies, Definition \ref{topologies-definition-zariski-covering})
of $V_j$. Then the pullback functor
$$
\text{descent data relative to }
\mathcal{V}
\longrightarrow
\text{descent data relative to }
\mathcal{U}
$$
of Lemma \ref{lemma-pullback-family} is an equivalence of categories.
In particular, the category of schemes over $S$
is equivalent to the category
of descent data relative to any Zariski covering of $S$.

review_note: Preserves that refinement of fpqc coverings yields fully faithful DD(V)→DD(U), and the embedding Sch/S→DD(U) is fully faithful. It correctly avoids claiming all fpqc scheme descent data effective.
statement: For a family $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to S\}$, let $\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal U)$ be the category of families of $U_i$-schemes $V_i$ together with isomorphisms $\varphi_{ij}:V_i\times_SU_j\xrightarrow{\sim}U_i\times_SV_j$ over $U_i\times_SU_j$ satisfying the cocycle condition on triple overlaps. A morphism of families $(\alpha,g_i):\mathcal U\to\mathcal V=\{V_j\to S\}$ comprises a function $\alpha:I\to J$ and maps $g_i:U_i\to V_{\alpha(i)}$ over $S$; it induces a pullback functor $\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal V)\to\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal U)$. Let $\mathcal U$ and $\mathcal V$ both be fpqc coverings of $S$, and suppose $\mathcal U$ refines $\mathcal V$. Then the induced pullback $\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal V)\to\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal U)$ is fully faithful. Consequently, for any fpqc covering $\mathcal U$ of $S$, the category $\operatorname{Sch}/S$ embeds fully faithfully into $\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal U)$ through canonical descent data. No assertion that this embedding is essentially surjective for all schemes is made.
hypotheses: Both covers fpqc and U refines V.
conclusions: Refinement pullback is fully faithful, and schemes over S embed fully faithfully into descent data on an fpqc cover.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-refine-coverings-fully-faithful}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to S\}_{i \in I}$, and
$\mathcal{V} = \{V_j \to S\}_{j \in J}$,
be fpqc-coverings of $S$.
If $\mathcal{U}$ is a refinement of $\mathcal{V}$,
then the pullback functor
$$
\text{descent data relative to }
\mathcal{V}
\longrightarrow
\text{descent data relative to }
\mathcal{U}
$$
is fully faithful.
In particular, the category of schemes over $S$
is identified with a full subcategory of the category
of descent data relative to any fpqc-covering of $S$.

review_note: Retains the fpqc singleton p:X→S with flatness, surjectivity and quasi-compactness, plus every point v of a descent datum V having an invariant open W with effective restricted datum. The full datum is then effective, with correct local-upstairs condition.
statement: Fix $p:X\to S$. Write $\mathrm{DD}(X/S)$ for the category of descent data for schemes along $X\to S$. An object is a scheme $V\to X$ and an isomorphism $\varphi:V\times_S X\xrightarrow{\sim} X\times_SV$ over $X\times_SX$ satisfying the cocycle identity on $X\times_SX\times_SX$. Morphisms are $X$-morphisms compatible with these isomorphisms. For a morphism $f:X'\to X$ over $S$, pullback is the functor $f^*:\mathrm{DD}(X/S)\to\mathrm{DD}(X'/S)$ taking $V$ to $V\times_X X'$ and $\varphi$ to its pullback along $f\times_Sf$. Let $p:X\to S$ be surjective, flat, and quasi-compact. Let $(V\to X,\varphi)$ be a descent datum relative to $X/S$. Say the datum is *effective* if it is isomorphic to the canonical pullback $(X\times_SU,\mathrm{can})$ of some scheme $U\to S$. Suppose every $v\in V$ has an open neighbourhood $W\subseteq V$ such that (i) the descent isomorphism preserves that open, $\varphi(W\times_SX)\subseteq X\times_SW$, so the restriction $\varphi|_{W\times_SX}$ defines descent data on $W$, and (ii) this restricted datum is effective. Then $(V,\varphi)$ itself is effective, by descending overlaps and gluing the resulting $S$-schemes.
hypotheses: X→S is an fpqc singleton cover; V with descent datum admits compatible open effective neighbourhoods covering V.
conclusions: The global descent datum is effective.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-effective-for-fpqc-is-local-upstairs}
Let $X \to S$ be a surjective, quasi-compact, flat morphism of
schemes. Let $(V, \varphi)$ be a descent datum relative to $X/S$.
Suppose that for all $v \in V$ there exists an open subscheme
$v \in W \subset V$ such that $\varphi(W \times_S X) \subset X \times_S W$
and such that the descent datum $(W, \varphi|_{W \times_S X})$
is effective. Then $(V, \varphi)$ is effective.
